title: Trump Names Conservative Commentator Katie Zacharia as New White House Press Secretary
snippet: President Donald Trump has chosen Katie Zacharia, a former Truth Social adviser and media commentator, as his next White House press secretary following a swift selection process.
content:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump has appointed conservative commentator and former administration official Katie Zacharia as the next White House press secretary, selecting a loyal ally to take over the podium in Washington.

Trump announced the hiring on Friday, highlighting Zacharia’s background with his media venture, Truth Social, as well as her frequent appearances on television news networks.

A Swift Search for Loyalty

Zacharia’s appointment came together rapidly. Sources familiar with the decision noted that she was not under active consideration as recently as last week. The White House had reportedly encountered difficulties while vetting higher-profile candidates, several of whom were ruled out after past critical remarks about the president came to light.

Before extending the offer, Trump sought input from trusted advisers, including former press secretary Karoline Leavitt, who offered her endorsement during the final deliberations.

Media Veteran Takes the Podium

Prior to her new role, Zacharia worked as a senior communications adviser for Trump Media & Technology Group and served briefly as a senior official at the Department of Homeland Security. Her political experience dates back to 2006, when she interned for the Republican National Committee during the George W. Bush administration, and she later served as a legal adviser for Fix California, an organization founded by Trump ally Richard Grenell.

Addressing the appointment on social media, Zacharia expressed gratitude to the president and signaled her eagerness to work with reporters.

“Serving President Trump and the American people at this critical 250-year mark is the honor of a lifetime,” Zacharia wrote on X, adding that she looks forward to communicating the administration's legislative and policy achievements to the national press corps.
